Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for Canada's response with the bat. The Italian players spread out to the field and take their spots. Yuvraj Samra and Dilpreet Bajwa are the two openers for Canada. Thomas Draca will open the attack for Italy. Here we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

The Canadian Fightback - Canada, though, executed their plans in the fag end of the innings to claw back the game under their control. Kaleem Sana, Dilpreet Bajwa, Jaskarandeep Singh and Saad Bin Zafar ended with a wicket apiece. 156 is not a big total but the Canadian batters will be tested under pressure. However, the ball is in their court and Italy have to start well with the new ball. Stay tuned for the chase.

Italy’s Aggressive Start - Italy took the initiative early, playing a proactive brand of cricket that put the Canadian opening bowlers on the back foot. The Italian top order found the boundary with regularity, utilizing the powerplay, scoring 51 runs and middle overs to build what looked like a daunting total. Their aggressive strike rotation and calculated risks suggested a final score well north of 180 with JJ Smuts and Harry Manenti in the middle.

A quick recovery from Canada -. After a dominant start from the Italian batters, Canada’s bowlers showed incredible resolve under pressure. Conceding just 40 runs in the final five overs. Italy played a fine innings for the better part of 15 overs, but they’ll be kicking themselves after the finish as a score of 180 was on the cards at the halfway mark.
Sneaks in a couple! Short of a length on middle, Benjamin Manenti swipes across and hits it to long on for a brace. Italy end with 156/4.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to begin. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Justin Mosca and Anthony Mosca are the two openers for Italy. Kaleem Sana has the new ball in hand. Let's go...

The captain of Italy - Wayne Madsen says they would have preferred to bowl first as well, taking the dew factor into account. He adds that the plan is to post a good total and then look to defend it. Madsen also mentions that the team had solid preparations for the tournament in the UAE and is eager to leave a lasting impression and announce Italy’s presence on the global cricketing stage.

The captain of Canada - Dilpreet Bajwa says the dew factor, along with similar conditions experienced during the pre-tour in Sri Lanka, makes bowling first the preferred option. He adds that it feels special to be playing on Indian soil and notes that the pitch looks good for batting. Bajwa says the focus will be on putting in a strong all round performance. When asked about the fixture he is most looking forward to in the main draw, he points to the opening game against South Africa, saying it will set the tone and give the team a clear idea of where they stand.

Canada - Dilpreet Bajwa (C), Navneet Dhaliwal, Nicholas Kirton, Ravinderpal Singh, Yuvraj Samra, Shivam Sharma, Saad Bin Zafar, Harsh Thaker, Dilon Heyliger, Ajayveer Singh, Kanwarpal Tathgur (WK), Shreyas Movva, Jaskarandeep Singh, Kaleem Sana, Ansh Patel.

Italy - Anthony Mosca, Harry Manenti, Syed Naqvi, Wayne Madsen (C), Justin Mosca, JJ Smuts, Grant Stewart, Benjamin Manenti, Gian-Piero Meade (WK), Marcus Campopiano, Crishan Kalugamage, Ali Hasan, Thomas Draca, Zain Ali, Jaspreet Singh
TOSS - Canada have won the toss and will BOWL first.

What's at stake? While warm-up matches don't carry official T20I status, the psychological edge is massive. Italy needs to prove they belong at this level before facing Group C giants like England and the West Indies. Canada, slotted in Group D with South Africa, New Zealand, and Afghanistan, needs to find a winning rhythm early to stand any chance of an upset in the main draw.

Italy, the new kids on the block - Italy’s qualification was the fairytale story of the European Qualifiers. Led by veteran Wayne Madsen, the 'Azzurri' have bolstered their ranks with professional experience. The headline addition of former South African international JJ Smuts gives Italy a massive boost in both the batting and spin departments.

Canada - The experienced campaigners - Canada enters the 2026 tournament with a squad that blends gritty experience with emerging talent. Now under the leadership of Dilpreet Bajwa, the Canadians are looking to refine their Powerplay strategy. Having been a regular feature in global qualifiers, they understand the pressure of these conditions. The likes of Nicholas Kirton and the former skipper Saad Bin Zafar will be important cogs in the wheel in that middle order, with the latter also being a handy spin bowling option.

Warm-up, Match 3 in Chennai - As the cricketing world turns its eyes to India and Sri Lanka for the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2026, the warm-up phase kicks off with a fascinating clash between two nations looking to make a statement. Canada and Italy meet in Match 3 of the official warm-up schedule, providing a vital dress rehearsal for the high-stakes tournament ahead. For Italy, this is more than just a practice match; it’s a historic step toward their maiden T20 World Cup appearance. Canada, meanwhile, returns to the world stage, aiming to build on their growing reputation as a dangerous Associate side.
